title: Fewer Tokens, Smaller Cache: Reward-Coordinated Efficient Reasoning
event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-08-05 on efficient LLM reasoning via reward-coordinated KV-cache compression and generation control
problem: Large Reasoning Models use long chain-of-thought reasoning which causes overthinking and high inference costs. Existing KV-cache compression methods apply uniform policies across the trajectory and ignore that compression tolerance varies along reasoning steps. Cache-only compression can backfire by lengthening generation, partially canceling intended savings.
mechanism: ReCo coordinates three components under a single process reward: (1) reward-adaptive KV-cache compression that shrinks cache harder at high-reward steps, (2) reward-banded penalty on reflection tokens to curb redundant generation, (3) confidence-based early stopping triggered when answer perplexity satisfies threshold. A lightweight process-reward estimator scores each completed step.

evidence.claim: ReCo achieves 2.08x-2.35x latency speedup over Full CoT across three reasoning models
evidence.condition: single NVIDIA H20 GPU, six reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH500, AMC, AIME24, AIME25, GPQA)

evidence.claim: ReCo reduces generated tokens by 37%-65% across models
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Qwen3-8B on six benchmarks

evidence.claim: ReCo uses 17.92GB peak GPU memory, a 37.7% reduction over full cache
evidence.condition: AIME25 benchmark, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, single H20 GPU

evidence.claim: ReCo achieves 60.2% average accuracy vs. 58.1% baseline at comparable latency
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, six-benchmark average, 26.88s latency vs. 28.29s baseline

evidence.claim: Cache-only baselines gain only modest speedups (1.09-1.33x) since inflated generation cancels per-token attention savings
evidence.condition: Llama-8B, cache-only compression methods (SnapKV, R-KV, RPC)

evaluation_context: Evaluated on three reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Qwen3-8B) across six math benchmarks from grade-school to competition level. Hardware: single NVIDIA H20 GPU. Metrics include accuracy, average tokens per problem, end-to-end wall-clock latency per problem, peak GPU memory.
limitations: Evaluation limited to math reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH500, AMC, AIME24, AIME25, GPQA). ReCo components add small overhead: Pilot scoring 0.60%, KV compression 0.11%, reflection penalty 1.24%, early stopping 1.98% of end-to-end time. Uses a 30M step-level reward estimator.
project_relevance: KV-cache compression is directly relevant to cross-domain transmission of reasoning model states. Reward-adaptive compression based on trajectory position suggests that compression tolerance varies along reasoning chain. Token reduction (37%-65%) translates to reduced transfer bandwidth. Memory reduction (17.92GB vs 28.78GB) affects cross-domain cache placement capacity. The mechanism shows how step-wise importance metrics (process reward) can guide compression policy, which could inform cross-domain cache selection and transfer prioritization.
